mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines the process of resolving a vector into components?

options.A: Breaking a vector into two perpendicular vectors whose vector sum equals the original vector.
options.B: Finding the magnitude of a vector by squaring its components.
options.C: Changing the direction of a vector without altering its magnitude.
options.D: Multiplying a vector by a scalar to obtain a new vector.

mcqs.answer: Breaking a vector into two perpendicular vectors whose vector sum equals the original vector.
mcqs.explanation: Resolving a vector means expressing it as the sum of two mutually perpendicular components (usually along x and y axes). Option A states this correctly. Option B describes finding magnitude, not resolution. Option C describes rotation, not resolution. Option D describes scaling, not resolution.

mcqs.question: A vector of magnitude 20 N makes an angle of 30° with the positive x‑axis. What are its rectangular components (Fx, Fy)?
mcqs.explanation: Fx = 20 cos30° = 20·√3/2 ≈ 17.3 N and Fy = 20 sin30° = 20·0.5 = 10 N. Option A matches these values. The other options swap the components or ignore the angle.

mcqs.question: Given components Ax = 8 m/s east and Ay = 6 m/s north, what is the magnitude and direction (angle measured north of east) of the resultant vector?

options.A: Magnitude 10 m/s, direction 36.9° north of east
options.B: Magnitude 14 m/s, direction 45° north of east
options.C: Magnitude 10 m/s, direction 53.1° north of east
options.D: Magnitude 8 m/s, direction 36.9° north of east

mcqs.answer: Magnitude 10 m/s, direction 36.9° north of east
mcqs.explanation: Resultant magnitude = √(8²+6²)=10 m/s. Direction θ = tan⁻¹(6/8)=36.9° north of east. Option A gives both correctly. Options B and C use wrong magnitude or angle; D has wrong magnitude.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: A ball is thrown with an initial speed of 25 m/s at an angle of 60° above the horizontal. Using the component method, what is the initial vertical component of velocity?
mcqs.explanation: Vy = 25 sin60° = 25·√3/2 ≈ 21.65 m/s, rounded to 21.7 m/s. Option A is correct. Option B is the horizontal component (25 cos60°). Options C and D are unrelated.

mcqs.question: A student claims that when a vector is resolved into components, the sum of the magnitudes of the components is always equal to the magnitude of the original vector. Is this statement correct?

options.A: No, because the component magnitudes add vectorially, not algebraically.
options.C: No, it is only true when the components are perpendicular.
options.D: Yes, but only if the vector lies along one of the axes.

mcqs.answer: No, because the component magnitudes add vectorially, not algebraically.
mcqs.explanation: The magnitudes of perpendicular components combine via the Pythagorean theorem, not by simple addition. Hence the sum of magnitudes is generally larger than the original magnitude. Option A states this correctly. Options B, C, and D are false statements.

mcqs.question: A force of 50 N acts at 120° measured counter‑clockwise from the positive x‑axis. Which of the following correctly gives its rectangular components (Fx, Fy)?
mcqs.explanation: Fx = 50 cos120° = 50·(-½) = -25 N. Fy = 50 sin120° = 50·(√3/2) ≈ 43.3 N. Option A matches these values. The other options have incorrect signs or swapped components.

mcqs.question: Two vectors A and B have components: A = (3 î + 4 ĵ) N, B = (‑3 î + 4 ĵ) N. Which statement correctly compares the magnitudes and directions of the resultant vectors when each is reconstructed from its components?

options.A: Both have the same magnitude of 5 N, but A points in the first quadrant while B points in the second quadrant.
options.B: Vector A has a larger magnitude than vector B.
options.C: Both vectors point in the same direction.
options.D: Both vectors have a magnitude of 7 N.

mcqs.answer: Both have the same magnitude of 5 N, but A points in the first quadrant while B points in the second quadrant.
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude of each = √(3²+4²)=5 N. A’s components are positive, placing it in the first quadrant (0°–90°). B’s x‑component is negative, y positive, placing it in the second quadrant (90°–180°). Hence option A is correct. Options B, C, D are false.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: A projectile is launched from ground level with speed 40 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance and taking g = 10 m/s², what is the horizontal range? (Use component method.)
mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component Vx = 40 cos37° ≈ 32 m/s. Vertical component Vy = 40 sin37° ≈ 24 m/s. Time of flight = 2Vy/g = 2·24/10 = 4.8 s. Range = Vx·t = 32·4.8 ≈ 153.6 m, rounded to 154 m. Option A matches. Other options result from incorrect component values or arithmetic.
